NEVER CLIMBS: core/policy/band_test.go::TestComposeForceCannotBreachNeverAutoFloor (even an operator FORCE override under the least-restrictive AUTO band clamps back to approve when the floor applies, and the clamp is recorded) + modules/actuation/ssh/mutate_test.go::TestNeverAutoFloorRefusedEvenIfAllowlisted (the leaf floors it whether or not it is allowlisted, and whether or not it is MIS-allowlisted). Three layers, because 'never climbs' has to hold at admission, at composition, and at the leaf — a class that could not be ratified high but could be composed high would still reach the estate.

scenarios.name: The dossier answers the five operator questions in order
The graduation console extends the existing ladder rather than adding a second one
Overlay classes carry a declared opcover exemption
scenarios.note: PENDING WORK, not a missing oracle, and currently VACUOUS. opcover's population is opschema.Specs() — the COMPILED-IN registry (7 op-classes today, 5 fault-provoked + 2 declared exemptions, reporting COVERED). Operator-ratified OVERLAY classes are loaded at runtime from opclass_ratified, so a build-time check structurally cannot see them: the day the first class is ratified, opcover keeps reporting COVERED over 7 embedded classes while an 8th AUTO-capable class exists outside its denominator. That is the wrong-denominator shape, latent, with a precise trigger. Measured live 2026-08-07: opclass_ratified holds 0 rows (0 live), and all 10 opclass_candidate rows are still `observing` — so nothing needs exempting yet and the gap cannot be observed. spec/opcover-exemptions.json declares reload-service and disk-grow only; neither is the overlay exemption naming the embed-export path this requirement asks for. Resolving it means BOTH the declaration and a guard that fires on the first ratification rather than on review.
